yaml.ticket-to-cited-reply:
name: Ticket to cited reply
description: Takes a support ticket, retrieves the best docs with the stored hybrid search template, and drafts a short reply that cites only those docs.
enabled: true
tags:
  - demo
  - vector-search
triggers:
  - type: manual
inputs:
  - name: ticket_id
    type: string
    default: T-1042
  - name: ticket_text
    type: string
    default: "Customer ticket: our vector index uses too much RAM at 3072 dimensions"
steps:
  - name: search_docs
    type: elasticsearch.request
    with:
      method: POST
      path: /docs-jina/_search/template
      body:
        id: demo_hybrid_docs
        params:
          query: "{{ inputs.ticket_text }}"
          size: 3
  - name: draft_reply
    type: ai.prompt
    with:
      systemPrompt: >-
        You draft support replies. Every sentence of the reply must be supported by the documentation excerpts provided.
        Do not add general knowledge, industry norms or performance claims that the excerpts do not state. If the excerpts
        only partly answer the question, answer that part and say what they do not cover. Never state a setting, number or
        version that is not in the excerpts. Cite only the docs whose content you actually used.
      prompt: >-
        Ticket {{ inputs.ticket_id }}: {{ inputs.ticket_text }}

        Documentation excerpts (JSON, best match first):
        {{ steps.search_docs.output.hits.hits | json }}

        Write a reply of at most 120 words. Then list the docs you used.
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          reply:
            type: string
          cited_docs:
            type: array
            items:
              type: object
              properties:
                title:
                  type: string
                section:
                  type: string
                version:
                  type: string
        required:
          - reply
          - cited_docs
yaml.sales-digest:
name: Sales digest
description: Runs ES|QL over the orders index for a window, has a model write a short digest from the numbers, and stores it in the sales-digests index.
enabled: true
tags:
  - demo
  - vector-search
triggers:
  - type: manual
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: 1d
inputs:
  - name: start
    type: string
    default: "2026-11-07T00:00:00Z"
  - name: end
    type: string
    default: "2026-11-14T00:00:00Z"
steps:
  - name: totals
    type: elasticsearch.esql.query
    with:
      format: json
      query: >-
        FROM orders
        | WHERE @timestamp >= "{{ inputs.start }}" AND @timestamp < "{{ inputs.end }}"
        | EVAL net = CASE(status == "cancelled" OR status == "returned", 0.0, line_total),
               is_returned = CASE(status == "returned", 1, 0),
               is_cancelled = CASE(status == "cancelled", 1, 0)
        | STATS lines = COUNT(*), orders = COUNT_DISTINCT(order_id), revenue = ROUND(SUM(net)),
                returned_lines = SUM(is_returned), cancelled_lines = SUM(is_cancelled)
  - name: top_categories
    type: elasticsearch.esql.query
    with:
      format: json
      query: >-
        FROM orders
        | WHERE @timestamp >= "{{ inputs.start }}" AND @timestamp < "{{ inputs.end }}" AND status != "cancelled" AND status != "returned"
        | STATS revenue = ROUND(SUM(line_total)) BY category
        | SORT revenue DESC
        | LIMIT 3
  - name: top_products
    type: elasticsearch.esql.query
    with:
      format: json
      query: >-
        FROM orders
        | WHERE @timestamp >= "{{ inputs.start }}" AND @timestamp < "{{ inputs.end }}" AND status != "cancelled" AND status != "returned"
        | STATS revenue = ROUND(SUM(line_total)), units = SUM(quantity) BY product = product_name.keyword
        | SORT revenue DESC
        | LIMIT 3
  - name: write_digest
    type: ai.prompt
    with:
      systemPrompt: >-
        You write a three-line sales digest for a retail team. Use only the figures provided and quote them exactly.
        Revenue excludes cancelled and returned lines. Never invent a figure or a comparison to another period.
      prompt: >-
        Window: {{ inputs.start }} to {{ inputs.end }}.
        Totals (columns and values): {{ steps.totals.output | json }}
        Top categories by revenue: {{ steps.top_categories.output | json }}
        Top products by revenue: {{ steps.top_products.output | json }}
        Write exactly three lines: overall result, the leading categories, the leading products.
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          digest:
            type: string
        required:
          - digest
  - name: store_digest
    type: elasticsearch.index
    with:
      index: sales-digests
      document:
        "@timestamp": "{{ execution.startedAt | date: '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' }}"
        window_start: "{{ inputs.start }}"
        window_end: "{{ inputs.end }}"
        digest: "{{ steps.write_digest.output.content.digest }}"
        revenue: "{{ steps.totals.output.values[0][2] }}"
        orders: "{{ steps.totals.output.values[0][1] }}"
        cancelled_lines: "{{ steps.totals.output.values[0][4] }}"
        returned_lines: "{{ steps.totals.output.values[0][3] }}"

tickets.text: Customer ticket: our vector index uses too much RAM at 3072 dimensions

inputs.ticket_text: Customer ticket: our vector index uses too much RAM at 3072 dimensions

content.reply: Thanks for reaching out. High RAM usage at 3072 dimensions is expected since full-precision (float32) vectors use 4 bytes per dimension, and HNSW index memory scales with both dimensions and the `m` parameter (roughly `nodes * (dimensions * 4 + m * 2 * 8)` bytes). To reduce memory, consider enabling quantization: scalar quantization (`sq8`) uses 1 byte per dimension with typically under 1% recall loss, or `sq4` at 0.5 bytes per dimension with 1-3% recall loss. For the largest reduction, product quantization (`pq`) is configurable but needs careful tuning. Always measure recall before and after enabling quantization using the `vforge bench recall` command, and keep rescoring enabled if you use `pq`.

tickets.text: Customer ticket: search got slower after we turned on quantization, is accuracy affected?

inputs.ticket_text: Customer ticket: search got slower after we turned on quantization, is accuracy affected?

hits.title: Slow Query Diagnosis with EXPLAIN Plans

content.reply: Thanks for reaching out. Quantization does involve a trade-off between storage/bandwidth savings and search accuracy, but it should generally not make search *slower* — if latency increased after enabling it, that's unexpected and worth investigating separately (e.g., check whether rescoring is enabled, since rescoring fetches extra candidates and recomputes exact scores, which adds work). On accuracy: each scheme has a typical recall loss (e.g., sq8 under 1%, sq4 1-3%, pq 2-8%, binary 5-15% without rescoring), but actual loss depends on your data. We recommend running the built-in recall benchmark (`vforge bench recall`) comparing your baseline to the quantized setting to measure the real impact, and keeping rescoring enabled for best accuracy. Could you confirm which quantization scheme and settings you're using?
